scope: Read-only contact data-flow review plus two private selected-plan contact replays; no estimator/controller change.

chain.details: Exact simulated qpos/qvel and known previously applied input feed momentum observer in these research runs. No robot sensing/noise/delay qualification.
Dynamics/momentum balance infers filtered net external generalized wrench. wrench() returns ground force/moment about wheel center; observer itself does not uniquely identify arbitrary contacts.

Intrinsic spherical wrench geometry + current wheel pose infer equivalent support point, shell/belt/rim records and load shares. Specialized rim sharing is supported; no general multiple-surface posterior.
ContactEstimator filters intrinsic normal and estimates friction from inferred slip; current measurements/geometry, not unknown future terrain.

Reads filtered normal/friction, locator-derived point and aggregate inferred normal load. It does not impose observed patch identity/load shares as future constraints or add native feedforward after successful MPC.

Plane orientation/point from estimates, bounded normal offset calibrated to aggregate inferred load at current measured state/applied input. No fictitious external support force; other wrench components not fitted.
Private mechanical/contact model integrates1ms steps on frozen estimated plane; predicted wheel/fork contact geometry, unilateral reaction and friction can change under candidate commands.

what_is_already_predicted: Future own-body/shell/belt/rim contact geometry with estimated local plane
Contact loss/recontact and multiple admitted private model contacts
Predicted frictional forces/sliding from mechanical model and assumed estimated coefficient
Nonwheel collisions (not rejected solely by current finite+bounded plan acceptance)
not_currently_provided: Unknown terrain ahead, step heights or a new remote ground normal
General simultaneous contacts on independent terrain surfaces
Contact-mode probability/confidence distribution or particle posterior
A guarantee predicted transitions match actual events under changed/replanned inputs
A generic feedforward guarantee from the raw observed contact point
important_limits: Selected-plan forecast is different from replaying actual later commands. Frequent replanning means its future contacts need not occur in Gazebo.
Private predicted contact forces are model outputs, never live Gazebo force inputs.
Single frozen plane/friction over.4s does not represent arbitrary off-road topology.
Sparse Jacobian interpolation can cross predicted mode changes, but this telemetry alone establishes no cause of drift.
